title: SI Edge common definitions (v0.1)
description: Shared definitions used by the other SI Edge v0.1 schemas: identifiers, timestamps, durations, digests, signatures, residency tags (SIE-RT section 11, TERMINOLOGY.md), and conformance profile tags (SIE-RT section 21, SIE-COM Part C, SIE-PRV section 11). Status: Draft, not for implementation.

schemaVersion.description: Schema version as MAJOR.MINOR. These schemas describe major version 0 (SIE-COM section A5: receivers reject unknown major versions).

identifier.description: Identity of an owner, device, agent, provider, module, or registry, expressed as a URI (for example a DID, SIE-COM section A2).

uri.description: Absolute URI. HTTPS is expected for network locations.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 date-time with an explicit offset or Z. In deterministic CBOR the same value MAY be carried as CBOR tag 1 (epoch seconds); see schemas/README.md (non-normative).

duration.description: ISO 8601 duration, for example PT0S (no retention), PT1H, P30D.

nonce.description: Random nonce, unpadded base64url, at least 128 bits (22 characters). The lower bound is a conservative choice, see schemas/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md.

signature.description: Signature over the canonical encoding (deterministic CBOR, RFC 8949 section 4.2, or JCS, RFC 8785) of the enclosing object with the sig member removed (SIE-COM section A5). The signature only proves who signed; trust in the key is established by identity statements (SIE-COM section A2).

alg.description: Signature algorithm, as a JOSE or COSE algorithm name (for example EdDSA, ES256, ML-DSA-65).

kid.description: Identifier of the signing key (for example a DID URL with a key fragment).

signer.description: Identity of the signer (agent, publisher, provider). REQUIRED for module and provider manifests so that the Core can show who signed (SIE-RT section 3).

canon.description: Canonical encoding the signature was computed over.

residencyTag.description: Residency tag (SIE-RT section 11). CH: Switzerland only. EU: EU and EEA member states only. CH-EU: Switzerland, or EU and EEA member states. Owner-defined tags use the x- prefix (conservative choice, see schemas/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md). Any tag a runtime or provider does not recognise MUST be treated as not allowed (fail closed); this schema only checks syntax.

dataClass.description: Data class label used by egress policy (SIE-RT section 11, section 13). No registered vocabulary exists yet (schemas/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md); lowercase dotted names such as health, contacts, location.precise are used in examples.

communicationProfile.description: C0 is a legacy hop, not a conformance profile (SIE-COM Part C).

amount.description: Decimal amount as a string to avoid floating point errors.
